---
title: "Bonus: Making it easier to log in to the cluster"
---

|                                                                       |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning Objectives:**                                              |
| Make logging in to Mantis easier |

So far logging in to Mantis has required significant typing: `ssh username@xanadu-submit-ext.cam.uchc.edu`. We can make this a little bit easier! We can edit a configuration file to create a shortcut (or several shortcuts) to the Mantis login node or the transfer node. 

### The SSH config

Because you set up SSH-key based authentication to get into Mantis, you should have a hidden directory on your *local machine* called `.ssh`. In that directory will be your SSH keys. 

For this we'll work with a file in that directory that is simply called `config`. 

Go to that directory now. If the file does not exist, create it with:

```bash
touch config
```

I'm going to suggest using `nano` to edit this file for now, but you can use any editor you like. 

```bash
nano config
```

Then enter:

```
Host mantis
Hostname login.hpc.cam.uchc.edu
User <your username>
ForwardX11 yes
SetEnv LANG=en_US.UTF-8
```

Remember to subsitute `<your username>` for your own username. 

`mantis` will be the name of the shortcut, you can change this if you want. You could cut it down to just `m` if you want to absolutely minimize typing. 

Now you should be able to log in with `ssh mantis`. 

You can set one of these up for the transfer node as well (this will work with `scp` and `rsync`:

```
Host transfer
Hostname transfer.hpc.cam.uchc.edu
User <your username>
```

And lastly, to prevent premature logouts

```Host *
    ServerAliveInterval 180
```
